text:
aj: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a hybrid prefetch+eviction layer for model weights. Goal: better cold-start for large sharded safetensors without blowing RAM or adding long synchronous warmups.

maria: curious — how is this different from the current warmup job + mmap path? :eyes:

aj: main differences: 1) we expose a tiny runtime policy that does partial mmap of index + async streaming of hot ranges, 2) eviction is shard-aware with heat tracking (per-key) instead of whole-file LRU, 3) we support prioritized warmup requests (prefix-based) and automatic downgrade to quantized variant if memory constrained.

simon: heat-tracking per-key sounds expensive. what's the cost?
aj: we only record coarse counters at shard-chunk granularity (e.g., 64KB chunk id). increment is atomic-u64 per chunk, aggregated periodically into the router. storage cost ~ (num_chunks)*8 bytes in the serving node — cheap for 128k chunk shards.

ethan: how do we handle safetensors? they don't support byte-range friendly maps unless we add an index, right?
aj: exactly. plan: keep a small on-disk index file (safetensors.idx) with tensor offsets. mmap the index only, not the whole weight file. Then stream ranges for requested chunks via HTTP/ib/posix reads. Index schema: tuple(tensor_name, offset, length, chunk_count).

lisa: can you paste the loader API sketch?
aj: sure:

```json
{
  "LoadOptions": {
    "mode": "partial|eager|lazy",
    "priority": "low|default|high",
    "allowed_variants": ["fp16","int8_q4","int8_q8"],
    "warmup_prefix_tokens": 64
  }
}
```

aj: runtime will: if mode=partial -> mmap index, async request first N chunks for tensors in warmup_prefix; if memory pressure -> evict low-heat chunks, try fallback variants.

maria: eviction policy specifics?
aj: eviction based on combined score = alpha*recency + beta*heat_inverse + gamma*size_penalty. defaults: alpha=0.5, beta=0.4, gamma=0.1. Tunable by tenant. We also cap per-GPU fragment allocation to avoid OOMs from fragmentation.

ethan: how do we measure correctness & perf for rollout?
aj: benchmarks: cold-start P95 latency for single-request sampling, sustained throughput under mixed small/long prompts, and token-cost delta when falling back to quantized variant. We'll add metrics: shard_chunk_loads, shard_evictions, avg_chunk_latency, warmup_hit_rate.

simon: integration with KV cache? if warmup prefetches KV pages we should mark them hot so subsequent decode uses GPU directly.
aj: agreed — warmup writes to GPU KV cache where possible. If streaming from remote, we first populate host-side staging, then async DMA into GPU. Failures fall back to smaller model variant automatically.

lisa: any security implications for streaming parts of weights over network?
aj: we use customer VPC private endpoints for Private/Dedicated. All transfers are TLS, mutual auth for remote object stores. Index-only mmap never contains secret material.

weights-bot: Deploy note: prototype branch is at github.com/redwood-inference/loader-proto/tree/hybrid-prefetch (perf numbers in README).

maria: rollout plan? feature flag + canary?
aj: yes. steps:
1) feature-flag gated in runtime (off by default).
2) Canary on internal dedicated pool with 2 tenants for 48h.
3) Measure metrics above + error budget.
4) Gradual % rollout to dedicated customers, then hosted tier if stable.

ethan: owner & followups?
aj: I'll own prototype + RFC PR. @maria will drive perf harness and metrics wiring. @simon to vet eviction edge cases. Opening PR now: github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/1234 :thumbsup:

lisa: small nit — need a graceful fallback API for callers to request "best-effort warmup" vs blocking warmup. please add to RFC.
aj: noted, adding param: blocking:true|false. blocking=true will stall request until warmup completes or timeout. blocking=false returns immediately and scheduler prioritizes warmup.

maria: sounds good. can we also expose a per-tenant budget for warmup io to avoid noisy neighbors?
aj: yes — quota + burst tokens. config example in PR.

simon: thanks. if no objections I'll +1 on RFC update after PR addresses blocking flag and quota.

aj: thanks all. I'll post short demo GIF and perf snapshot in the thread tomorrow.
